key_insight: A chiral 2D halide perovskite can detect telecom-band circularly polarized light through a hidden, giant third-order nonlinear circular dichroism revealed only by polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation.
engineering_relevance: This points to a route for wavelength-relevant CPL sensing, optical encryption, and anti-counterfeiting devices using perovskite nonlinear optics.
method: Measure polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation in orthogonal output channels.
Compare total-THG vs channel-separated THG to expose hidden opposite-handed chiral responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 when hidden chiral contributions are separated, whereas conventional total-THG analysis underestimates the effect.
watch_item: Device performance may look weaker if evaluated only by total THG intensity, so polarization-resolved characterization is essential for correct implementation and comparison.
paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
